clue.text: Love interest in adventure movie? She's enthralled

definitions.meaning: read as ..., the girl a James Bond film pairs with its spy hero
a female slave or serf, held in bondage or thrall

explanation.definitionFit: A bondswoman is a woman in bondage; split, the word also names a Bond girl from the spy films.

clue.text: Peculiar bulge on a sturgeon

indicators.note: something peculiar is odd, so the word bulge is put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd swelling is found on a big fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar' signals the rearrangement of the swelling's letters; 'on' just joins the two pieces, and the beluga is also the name of a white whale, though here it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a large sturgeon of the Caspian and Black Seas, prized for its caviar.

clue.text: All things considered, the French are annoying

definitions.note: a plural verb phrase, matched by the plural verb form meaning they irritate

parts.note: nett, the British spelling of net, is what remains after everything is taken into account
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: Overall, French people are irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a plural verb: the French 'nettle', meaning they 'are annoying' to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle is to irritate or provoke, from the stinging plant, so nettling people means irritating them.

clue.text: Having drunk Pils, grannies go for a cocktail

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: After downing their lager, the grandmothers move on to a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges PILS, GRANNIES and GO. 'drunk' reads as the past of drink, with Pils (a pale lager) the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Singapore Sling is a gin-based cocktail with cherry brandy, created at Raffles Hotel.

clue.text: Charge at place for filming

definitions.meaning: read as ..., present where a film is being shot

explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault or attack; split, it says on a film set.

clue.text: Musician first to moonwalk?

definitions.meaning: Louis ..., the jazz trumpeter and singer
Neil ..., the first person to walk on the Moon

explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to the jazz trumpeter Louis and to the astronaut Neil.

clue.text: Clouseau perhaps occupies most of movie

indicators.note: only most of the word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a flick is an informal word for a film

explanation.surface: A bumbling detective takes up the greater part of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the last letter, K, from FLICK. Inspector Clouseau is the French policeman of the Pink Panther films, and FLIC is French slang for a cop.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouseau is a French police inspector, and flic is French slang for a policeman, so he is an example.

clue.text: He'll seduce woman unwilling with a port

parts.note: loth, also spelt loath, means reluctant
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A seducer persuades a reluctant woman with a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' sounds like the wine, but it is a harbour city, Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: A lothario is a womaniser, named after a seducer in an 18th-century play.

clue.text: They may hold drink — are youngsters able to?

parts.note: can means is or are able to
teens are teenagers

explanation.surface: A question about whether teenagers are allowed to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a container, not a person: water bottles carried by soldiers or campers.
explanation.definitionFit: Canteens are flasks for carrying water, so they hold liquid to drink.

clue.text: Offices provide targets for pirates without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the ships go round the resistance

parts.note: treasure ships are galleons laden with gold that pirates preyed on
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Bureaucrats give pirates easy prey when nobody resists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the pirates' prey wraps round the resistance symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurership is the post of treasurer, an office in a society or company.

clue.text: Some plutonium found in airport

indicators.note: only some of the word plutonium is used, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: Traces of a radioactive metal are detected at an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: LUTON is an airport north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Luton is the site of London Luton Airport, so the town's name serves for the airport.

clue.text: Sort of saint taking in one with damage

definitions.text: Sort of saint taking in one with damage

indicators.note: the shuffled word takes the other pieces inside itself, as a container
a sort of saint is a rearranged version of the word, so its letters are shuffled

parts.note: A is a single one, the indefinite article
to mar is to damage or spoil

explanation.surface: A charitable person, a kind of saint, takes in someone who has been injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' signals the shuffle and 'taking in' the container. Read whole, the clue also tells the parable of the Good Samaritan, who cared for a beaten traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: In the parable the Samaritan rescued a beaten traveller, so a good-hearted helper of the injured is a saintly figure.

clue.text: Noble with ill-will to member of army

parts.note: gall is bitterness or rancour
ants live in colonies sometimes called armies, so one ant is a member

explanation.surface: An aristocrat bears a grudge against a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member of army' looks like a soldier, but it is an insect: ants march in armies.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant describes chivalrous, high-minded conduct, a synonym for noble in its sense of honourable.

clue.text: Wood, pine's sound — one may toast it

indicators.note: the clue asks for how the two words come out when spoken together

parts.note: teak is a hardwood and to pine is to ache with longing, giving teak ache

explanation.surface: A remark about the timber and resin of a pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' signals that TEAK plus ACHE, run together, is heard as the name of a bun. 'pine' looks like the tree beside 'Wood', but here it is the verb meaning to long or ache.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a sweet currant bun usually split and toasted before buttering.

clue.text: TV serial the answer for film producer

parts.note: a soap opera, or soap, is a long-running television serial
a solution is the answer to a problem

explanation.surface: A television drama turns out to be the key for a movie mogul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film producer' suggests a movie mogul, but the film is the thin skin of a soap bubble.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapy water is what makes the thin membrane in bubble blowing, so it produces a film.

clue.text: Legislator comes in to support man's climbing plant

indicators.note: the legislator enters the support, going inside it

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch
an MP, a Member of Parliament, makes laws

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means read upwards, so the name is reversed

parts.note: Len is a man's name

explanation.surface: An MP joins in to prop up a fellow's creeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' looks like it describes the plant but tells you to read the man's name upwards in this down entry; 'comes in' signals the container. The scarlet pimpernel is not in fact a climber.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is a small wildflower with red blooms that close in dull weather.

clue.text: Dinosaur wanting capital punishment almost on demand

indicators.note: almost the whole phrase is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: the rope is a byword for hanging, the death penalty
OD is a standard abbreviation for on demand

explanation.surface: A fossil beast lacks demand for the death penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final E of THE ROPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A theropod is a two-legged meat-eating dinosaur such as T. rex.

clue.text: Mine's terrible place for fragile material

parts.note: egg was wartime slang for a bomb or mine, so the mine is an egg
hell is the archetypal place of torment

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their mine is a dreadful place to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like a pit or a possessive, but it is an explosive, called an egg in old service slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell is a thin brittle covering, and the word is used for anything delicate or easily cracked.

clue.text: Secret proposal in Cameron's speech?

definitions.meaning: clandestine or hushed-up, as in hole-and-corner dealings
read as 'hug a mugger', echoing the 'hug a hoodie' line the press gave a 2006 David Cameron speech on youth crime

explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron, later UK Prime Minister, gave a 2006 speech urging understanding of hooded youths, which the press dubbed 'hug a hoodie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugger-mugger is an old word for concealment or furtive secrecy, and split it echoes a tabloid summary of a political speech.

clue.text: A coin's wasted here?

indicators.note: wasted suggests something wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: the words read as written, the S included

explanation.surface: Is this where money gets frittered away?
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' rearranges A COINS; the whole clue also describes a gambling hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a gambling house, where stakes are often lost.

clue.text: Platform — one for English in upper classes

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: the gentry are the well-born classes below the nobility
A is a single one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A stage where someone stands in for an Englishman among the upper crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the E of GENTRY for A; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gantry is a raised framework bridging a space, used as a working platform for cranes or rockets.

clue.text: Decide to answer clue again

definitions.meaning: to make up one's mind firmly
read as ..., to work out a puzzle a second time

explanation.definitionFit: To resolve is to determine on a course; split, it means to solve a second time.

clue.text: Cosmetic old lady has to cover a blemish

indicators.note: the mother and the A wrap around the blemish, covering it

parts.note: one's old lady is one's mother, MA
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: Grandma uses make-up to conceal a mark on her face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' signals the container, with the mother and the article wrapped round the mark; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is make-up for darkening the eyelashes.

clue.text: Dignitary dressing right

parts.note: mayo is short for mayonnaise, a salad dressing

explanation.surface: A grandee gets dressed properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests putting on robes, but it is a salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the civic head of a town, a dignitary wearing a chain of office.

clue.text: Woman following 1996/7 car for a time carrying a child

indicators.note: the woman's name comes after the car, following it

parts.note: British number plates registered from August 1996 to July 1997 began with P, so such a car is a P-reg
Nancy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman tailing an old car for a while has a baby on board.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK, cars were dated by a registration letter: P covered August 1996 to July 1997, so a car of then is 'P-reg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pregnancy is the period during which a woman is expecting, the months of gestation.

clue.text: Gull — one I point out

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: out signals the letters put together in a different arrangement

parts.note: a dot is a small point

explanation.surface: A seabird, as one person points out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I, I and DOT. 'Gull' looks like the seabird but is the verb or noun for a dupe, someone easily fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is an old word for a dupe or simpleton, someone easily fooled, so a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Give out grief

definitions.meaning: an archaic and poetic word for sorrow or lamentation

explanation.definitionFit: To dole is to hand out shares; as a noun, dole is an old poetic word for sorrow.

clue.text: Ely rector's arranged high position in church

indicators.note: the clergyman's letters are arranged in a new order

parts.note: the words read as written, the S included

explanation.surface: A cathedral clergyman at Ely has his top post sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles ELY RECTORS. 'high position' sounds like rank, but it is literal height: the upper level of a church's nave wall. ELY is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The clerestory is the upper storey of a church nave, pierced with windows above the aisle roofs.
